topics.topic: Audit coverage for accepted, refused, and agent-authority state-changing actions
questions: For every primary action, which accepted and refused outcomes produce an audit entry—especially room creation, pointer publication or withdrawal, session registration, pending requests, request answers, active-project changes, relationship end/resume and imports—and does “agent calls” exclude state-changing agent calls?

Which changed actions count as audited “changes to projects”: room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, import, archiving, session registration, access requests and answers, and active-project changes?
Are successful state-changing agent-authority calls recorded in the audit log, or does the exclusion of “agent calls” cover writes as well as reads?
Which primary actions count as significant changes—specifically room changes, artifact publication or withdrawal, imports, session registration, pending access requests and active-project changes?
Does the audit log contain refused or failed attempts at significant changes, or only accepted changes that altered state?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which accepted, refused and state-changing actions produce audit entries.

precedent.topic: Which accepted, refused, and state-changing actions produce audit entries
quotes:
Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and
customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects,
restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations. Ordinary reads, agent calls and the inner steps of flows
are not recorded in Registry; security events of the infrastructure are
handled by the infrastructure, outside Registry.

- **Audit.** A minimal log of significant changes of state (R0-58): time, the
  acting principal (owner, which service, agent through Kernel), the change,
  the project or customer, the outcome, the contract and release version, and
  a confirmation id where the owner confirmed.
precedent.why: The exact event-selection and outcome-recording criteria are operational rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: When imported projects require replacement display names and whether legacy names may remain
questions: Is a new display name mandatory for every imported project, mandatory only when the legacy name identifies a person, or always optional?
Must every imported project receive a replacement display name, or may its legacy display name be retained, including one containing a person's name?
For each selected project, when is a replacement display name mandatory, and may an imported project retain its old display name?

quotes:
When the owner picks the projects to import, the owner may give each a new
display name and an alias (R0-82); the project arrives under them, its id kept.

The owner names a project by its object and work, never by a person: the
customer's name lives in its Customer record.

Projects imported
under a person's name (R0-79) are renamed by the owner after the import.

Narrowed by R0-85: they are renamed in the import itself, which also reaches
archived projects.
judgement.why: A replacement name is generally optional, but a legacy name identifying a person must be replaced during import.

topics.topic: Which customer fields survive customer-data erasure
questions: When customer contact data is erased, are kind, tax id, legal name, restriction state and relationship-end date also removed, or do any of them survive?
When this action erases a Customer, are tax id and legal name erased too, or do they remain stored?
When the owner erases a customer's contact data, are tax id, legal name, kind, restriction state and relationship-end date also removed, or does some of that data survive?

judgement.why: This is the same question about which customer and fiscal fields survive erasure.

precedent.topic: Which customer and fiscal fields survive customer erasure
quotes:
Erasing a customer's contact data (R0-06) is the end of its record: the
Customer keeps its identity and the fact that it was erased, and projects keep
naming it. There is no action that deletes a Customer whole.
precedent.why: Because the erased Customer keeps only its identity and erased fact, kind, tax id and legal name do not survive.

topics.topic: Agent-session access-version initialization and changes, including repeated access operations
questions: Which actions change the access version, what is its initial value, and do idempotent grants, replacement requests, declines, active-project changes and no-op revocations advance it?
What is the access version's concurrency contract across registration, grants, revocations, active-project changes, access requests and answers?
What observable result, access-version effect and audit effect do these repeated session-access requests have?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously judged question about the session access version's initialization, transitions and concurrency contract.

precedent.topic: Meaning and concurrency contract of the session access version
quotes: the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.
precedent.why: Mutation preconditions, version-transition rules and stale-input behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Expected-revision requirements, revision advancement, and stale-change failures
questions: Must archive, customer erasure, restriction changes, relationship end/resume and archived-project erasure state an expected revision and fail when stale, and what revision does each successful action return?
Exactly which primary actions must carry an expected project or customer revision, which actions advance it, and which stale attempts are refused?

judgement.why: This is the same question about mutation revision preconditions, advancement and stale-input behavior.

precedent.topic: Concurrency preconditions and stale-revision behavior for mutations
quotes:
Every change carries CSRF protection and
is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
(R0-35).

A project, a customer and an object carry a revision that every accepted change
moves. A change states the revision it was made against; a change against an
older revision is refused and nothing changes. Every change is atomic.

Narrowed by R0-45: the object has no revision of its own; a change of it moves
the project's.
the session's granted project ids, its active project if any, whether it has a pending request, and the access version — no `personal_data` value (R0-32, R0-46, R0-64)
precedent.why: Mapping expected versions to mutations, defining version advancement and specifying stale or idempotent behavior are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Owner sign-in action, success result, and credential-failure behavior
questions: What action accepts an unauthenticated sign-in request, what does a successful sign-in return or establish, and what observable failure is returned for a wrong credential?
What action signs the owner in, what does success establish or return, and what happens when the credential is absent or wrong?

judgement.why: This repeats the previously answered question about authentication of sign-in and the protected owner session it creates.

precedent.topic: Which owner-interface requests and response data are allowed before authentication
quotes: No operation of Registry answers an unauthenticated caller. The owner signs in to the owner interface (R0-30); each service — PresuPro, Client Portal, Cabinet, Cabinet Kernel — holds its own service token, which names it and the operations and highest disclosure class it may use.
There is one human principal, the owner. The owner signs in to the owner interface with the owner credential and gets a protected session; the session and its expiry belong to State 2.
precedent.why: No unauthenticated owner-interface request may answer; the sign-in request is authenticated with the owner credential and then creates the protected session.

topics.topic: Personal-data classification and guarantees for agent-visible free-text fields and display names
questions: Does Registry guarantee that no actual personal data reaches an agent, or only that fields classified by Registry as `personal_data` are withheld even though aliases, room names and pointer values may contain personal data?
Is a project's display name explicitly part of the `personal_data` class at this trust boundary?

quotes:
It holds no owner credential and no Registry
service token, never receives a value Registry holds as `personal_data` (R0-26;
for free text written by others see R0-68), and has no
administrative access to the production host, its store, configuration,
secrets or deployment (R0-25).

Registry does not inspect these values:
the rule binds their writers and is not a check of Registry, and a value that
breaks it is not refused and does reach the agent. Registry's own guarantee
(R0-26) covers every value it holds as `personal_data`.

A name such as "Reforma Pedreres
35" still carries a private object's address, which can identify a person, so
the display name is held as `personal_data`: it reaches the owner and a service
cleared for `personal_data` (R0-43), never the agent, and a consumer reads it
when it uses it instead of keeping it.
judgement.why: Registry withholds values it holds as `personal_data`, explicitly including display names, while uninspected writer-controlled aliases, room names and pointer values may violate their writer rules and still reach the agent.

topics.topic: Valid audit-erasure cutoffs and survival of the newly created erasure entry
questions: May the owner give today or a future date, and if so does the newly created erasure entry survive even when its timestamp is older than the supplied cutoff?
May the owner give a future cutoff date, which would make the newly created erasure entry itself older than the cutoff, and what is the observable failure for an invalid cutoff?

quotes: | erase audit entries before a date | owner, confirming | every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone; the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date (R0-66) | — |

The audit log's period is the governance's. In the periodic review the owner
erases, confirming, every entry older than a date the owner gives; that erasure
leaves an entry of its own naming the date. Registry erases no entry on its own.
judgement.why: Cutoff validation, operation ordering and the treatment of the newly created entry are rules and required tests owned by State 2.

topics.topic: Accepted WhatsApp contact-handoff behavior and whether it needs a dedicated action
questions: Which of these two behaviours is the accepted product behaviour, and does Registry need a dedicated owner-interface action for it?

topics.topic: Failure and pending-request behavior when answering an access request with an invalid or duplicate grant
questions: When answering a pending request with a grant, what happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised or already granted, and is the pending request cleared when that grant fails?

topics.topic: Handling imported artifact pointers with unknown types or mismatched owner services
questions: What happens if an imported pointer has an undeclared artifact type or names an owner service different from the specification's owner for that type?

topics.topic: How audit entries identify affected records without storing personal values
questions: How can an audit entry identify the affected project or customer while containing no personal value: does it store their ordinary identifiers, a non-reversible audit identifier, or only an entity type without a record reference?

topics.topic: How the owner obtains the current customer revision
questions: Through which owner-visible output does the owner obtain the current Customer revision required for a change?

topics.topic: No-op, revision, and audit behavior for repeated customer restriction changes
questions: Are repeated restriction or lift requests successful no-ops or failures, and do they advance the Customer revision or create audit entries?

topics.topic: Required review or replacement of legacy agent-visible room and pointer values
questions: Before imported rooms and pointer values can enter an agent projection, must the owner review or replace legacy values that were created before the writer rule existed?

topics.topic: Result of registering an agent session that already exists with state
questions: What does registration return when the session already exists and already has grants, an active project or a pending request?

topics.topic: Whether artifact pointers grant retrieval capability and how personal data is protected
questions: Are `uri` and `payload_ref` merely non-secret identifiers, or can either act as a capability that lets the agent or its external AI provider retrieve the service-owned artifact; if retrieval is possible, which boundary prevents access to personal data?

topics.topic: Whether billing-data reads include the customer's ordinary name
questions: Does the billing-data read return the customer's ordinary name to PresuPro, or is that name excluded along with all other contact data?

topics.topic: Which imported non-identity state is preserved versus initialized in production
questions: Which non-identity state is preserved from the VPS export, and which values are initialized by production during import?
